# Findings

## 29-01 — Selected outcomes and their verification do not agree
Severity: changes served wording and assessment metadata.

ODYSSEY OUTCOMES supplies primary MACE HR 0.85 (0.78–0.93). Its D5 object instead
selects a registered secondary CHD-death-only outcome, matched=true by
text_identity. The actual primary definition is already held in that D5 input.
The two are not the same endpoint. The current numerical row is not shown wrong.

FOURIER's selected 0.80 (0.73–0.88) is its key secondary three-point endpoint.
Older five-point-primary descriptions still appear in the current compatibility
notice. The familiar primary HR 0.85 must not be substituted just to fit that
stale description. Corrections should propagate the actual selected result's
endpoint and source through every assessment and disclosure.

## 29-02 — LONG TERM's evidence states are conflated
Severity: changes served wording and refusal-audit classification.

The post hoc cardiovascular result remains appropriately excluded by the written
policy. Finding HR 0.52 (0.31–0.90) does not disprove a post-hoc exclusion. The
reason-audit's value-present verdict is not an adjudication of the stated rule.

The injection-reaction row is currently blocked by a source-digest approval
mismatch. The source and signed notice describe a reported outcome. An
unreported-outcome label misstates that situation; preserve the approval block
while recording its actual reason. No reinstatement was attempted.

## Known issue followed up — VESALIUS binding
Not a newly discovered trial or defect. The earlier background-sentence binding
failure persists. The current source includes the actual co-primary definitions.
The three-point candidate's conditional addition gives HR 0.810647 with HKSJ
95% CI 0.703249–0.934446. The four-point alternative gives 0.821348
(0.729875–0.924285). Neither is an approved update. They must not be combined as
independent inputs or selected according to which result is more favorable.

## Clinical interpretation limits

The currently selected pool combines FOURIER's CV-death/MI/stroke endpoint with
ODYSSEY's CHD-death/MI/ischemic-stroke/unstable-angina-hospitalization endpoint.
The page discloses endpoint heterogeneity. This audit does not newly allege that
heterogeneity was hidden, nor does a generic MACE label make the inputs exact
matches. Each source population, time horizon and outcome definition must remain
attached. The current point estimate's direction is not an all-cause-mortality
conclusion or an absolute benefit estimate.
